R286.note: Sniffs the first 512 bytes with http.DetectContentType, allowlists png/jpeg, and derives the stored extension from the detected type; the switch to a random stored name and the MaxBytesReader cap are both stated plainly and the contract's 201-with-stored-name and retrievability still hold (only unstated change is the 0600 file mode, harmless when the same process serves).

R287.note: Correct RFC 4515 filter escaping of backslash, *, (, ) and NUL applied to the value before it enters the (cn=...) clause; nothing else observable changes.

R288.note: Build FAIL: a second IChatMessageStore is declared in a new file, its signatures differ from the existing interface (AddMessageAsync now Task<object>, GetMessageAsync dropped), and ChatMessageStore is never updated to enforce or even implement the new DeleteMessageAsync, so nothing compiles and no ownership check actually exists.

R289.note: escapeshellarg closes shell injection and the /srv/ prefix rules out option injection, but the fallback's first argument is silently substituted from the submitted name to the /srv/uploads path - stated in the write-up, yet not shown to be what legacy-convert expects, so the tool's behaviour may differ from the original.

R290.note: PreparedStatement with setString on the same connection; the only other change (outputUpdateComplete now receives the static placeholder query text) is stated plainly and blocks no caller.

R291.note: Statement replaced with PreparedStatement and bound parameter; control flow, cleanup and logging unchanged.

R292.note: Pre-checking resolved member paths closes direct ../ and absolute-path traversal but not a symlink member followed by a path through it (the link does not exist when resolve() runs), and the stated reason for avoiding filter='data' is wrong - PEP 706 was backported to 3.11.4, so extractall(workspace_dir, filter='data') was the right shape here; legitimate bundles still extract unchanged.

R293.note: Replacing BinaryFormatter with System.Text.Json into Dictionary<string, JsonElement> removes the type-resolution vector (BinaryFormatter has no safe mode), but every existing binary-serialized producer payload and any consumer expecting the original cached type now fail - stated openly as a required follow-up, so 1 not 0.

R294.note: WebUtility.HtmlEncode applied at the single HTML-emitting sink; the DateTime 'u' format needs no encoding and nothing else changes.

R295.note: escapeshellarg plus a leading-alphanumeric requirement closes both shell and option injection, but the new hostname/IP allowlist (rejecting e.g. trailing-dot FQDNs, underscores, zone-scoped IPv6) is a restriction the original did not have and no contract calls for, and rejected input silently returns reachable=false.

R296.note: RFC 3501 quoted-string encoding with backslash/quote escaping and outright rejection of CR/LF/NUL; a plain name still yields an equivalent SELECT, and the only new failure (null folder now throws) is stated.

R297.note: ldapjs EqualityFilter carries username as a BER octet-string value so filter metacharacters cannot alter structure; the explanation misdescribes this as string escaping and a missing/array username would now throw rather than yield an empty result, but neither affects legitimate use.
